notes: Main disagreements: (1) document stance for the ISC guidance, A delegates vs B permit; resolved to permit because it opens by embracing AI and sets only conditions, with course rules as an added layer. (2) Modality wording: should vs must vs may for advisory sentences, resolved by the source verb ("might consider" = may, "should be cited" = should, "up to you to decide" = must). The data-input rule was should-not (source: "should not input ... without"), with the policy rewritten to keep every listed condition. (3) Phase on general vs during-work/before-course statements, resolved by whether the sentence sets a step in the work or describes options. (4) Policy type on a few units (P56 vs P02 welcome sentence; P28 vs P45; P66 vs P83; P104 vs P31), resolved by comparing the passage with the type definitions. (5) Unit stance: coders split between neutral and permit/encourage/require for disclosure and mentoring lines; resolved to neutral unless the passage itself allows or restricts AI use. Coverage: coder A found 7 units B missed in the CETLI page (one dropped as duplicate list item merged into the study-use unit); B found 4 units A missed, all kept. Phase is a mismatch on pairs where one coder chose general; matched units were aligned by passage and rule.
